expanded_sentences: The patient is a 47-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
She has been previously treated with endocrine therapy for her breast cancer.
The patient experiences mild, ongoing cancer-related fatigue during systemic therapy.
Initially, she was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast at the age of 45.
Liver lesions consistent with metastatic disease were identified at 46 years and 6 months.
The breast carcinoma is classified as Stage IV with a TNM classification of T3, N1, M1.
A core biopsy of the primary breast lesion confirmed invasive ductal breast carcinoma.
A core biopsy of the hepatic lesion confirmed metastatic breast carcinoma.
Tumor profiling identified a PIK3CA mutation, which is relevant for targeted treatment selection.
The patient is currently receiving fulvestrant intramuscularly and palbociclib orally.
An MRI was performed on February 18, 2026, as part of her ongoing assessment.
The CA 15-3 level was elevated at 86.4 units per milliliter during the progression assessment.
The patient's maternal aunt, who is alive, had a history of breast cancer diagnosed at 52 years of age.
